elements.element: Customer is not liable for any liquidated damages under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that Customer “shall not be liable for any liquidated damages ... under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer is not liable for any penalties under the Agreement.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly states that Customer “shall not be liable for any ... penalties under this Agreement.”

elements.element: A liquidated amount may be charged to Customer only upon early termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause prohibits every liquidated amount payable by Customer, which is more protective than limiting such amounts to the early-termination context.

elements.element: The aggregate early-termination fee payable by Customer may not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is permitted under the rendered clause; therefore Customer's possible fee is zero and cannot exceed three months' fees.

elements.element: No liquidated damages or penalties other than the permitted early-termination fee are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause expressly prohibits all liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer, thereby excluding all other liquidated amounts.

result.reason: The redline cleanly replaces the dependency-delay liquidated-damages obligation with an agreement-wide prohibition on liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer. It fully achieves the preferred position and, as a more protective result, also stays within the fallback's maximum permitted exposure. The change is limited to the targeted liability and does not purport to eliminate otherwise available actual-damages remedies.
